`withRateLimit` in `src/middleware/index.js:19-24,84-107` uses **one shared counter for the entire process** — every caller, regardless of identity, draws from the same 30-requests-per-60-seconds budget:

```js
let windowStartedAt = Date.now();
let hitsInWindow = 0;
```

So "a few users sending two or three requests each" is exactly the failure mode: their requests all land in the same global bucket, and once *anyone's* combined traffic crosses 30/minute, the next caller — who may have sent only one request themselves — gets a 429. It's not a per-user limit malfunctioning; there is no per-user limit at all.

Notably, `src/store.js` already partitions notes per-owner (`listNotes(owner)`), so a per-user throttle is consistent with the rest of the codebase's design — this one piece just wasn't built that way.

One wrinkle: the chain in `server.js` currently runs `withRateLimit` **before** `withIdentity`, so `req.user` isn't available yet at throttle time. Fixing this properly means either reordering the chain (identity before throttle) or keying on something else. I'll work through that tradeoff as part of the plan.

Update `server.js`'s `CHAIN` order (`withIdentity` before `withRateLimit`) so the throttle has an identity to key on. Update `listNotes`'s call to `rateLimitSnapshot` to pass the caller's user. **Why reordering is safe:** the doc-comment's stated intent for throttle-before-identity was "a throttled request costs us no parsing" — identity resolution is a cheap header read, not the expensive part (JSON body parsing is). Moving identity first preserves that intent: an over-limit request still never reaches `withJsonBody`. It does mean an *unidentified* request (missing `x-user`) no longer gets rate-limited before its 401 — it consumes no quota at all, which is arguably more correct, not less.

**Test strategy:** update `test/notes.test.js` — add a test proving two different users each get their own full window (e.g., user A can spend their whole window while user B is unaffected).
